title: Devilled Kidneys
subtitle: Lamb kidneys in a hot, mustardy sauce on toast
excerpt: A Victorian breakfast classic: lamb kidneys quickly cooked in a fiery sauce of mustard, Worcestershire, and cayenne, then piled on thick toast. Sharp, rich, and done in ten minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Devilled kidneys were a fixture of the Victorian and Edwardian breakfast table, appearing regularly in Mrs Beeton and in the breakfast recipes of country houses where the sideboard held a selection of hot dishes. The word devilled in British cooking denotes a dish made fiery with mustard, cayenne, and Worcestershire sauce: a combination that appears across the Victorian repertoire in devilled bones, devilled turkey legs, and devilled whitebait. Kidneys were a preferred breakfast ingredient because they cooked very quickly and were cheap: the full English breakfast of that era was a much more varied meal than its modern form suggests. The dish declined with the decline of the staffed kitchen and the fading of the British tradition of elaborate breakfasts, but has experienced a revival through nose-to-tail restaurants and the renewed interest in offal.

content.text: Lamb kidneys must be very fresh and cooked quickly over high heat: 2 to 3 minutes per side maximum. Overcooked kidneys turn rubbery and develop an unpleasant ammonia edge. Remove the white core and membrane before cooking; this is the part that tastes strongest. The sauce must go in after the kidneys are cooked and the pan is off the heat: cooking the mustard too long makes it bitter.

items.preparation: halved, white core removed, membrane peeled off

content.text: In a small bowl, mix together the Dijon mustard, English mustard, Worcestershire sauce, cayenne, and lemon juice. Set aside.

Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat until very hot. Add the butter. When it foams, add the kidney halves cut-side down. Cook for 2 minutes without moving them. Turn and cook for a further 1 to 2 minutes: the kidneys should be coloured on the outside but still slightly pink in the centre.

Remove the pan from the heat. Pour in the mustard mixture and toss the kidneys quickly to coat. Return to the heat for 30 seconds, just to warm the sauce. Spoon over the toast, scatter with parsley, and serve immediately.
